vocabulary.pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness: Pronunciation: /k/ in "can" and /s/ in "sun". Phonemic awareness: Blending of spoken phonemes to form one-syllable and two-syllable words, such as blending /s/ /ʌ/ /n/ sounds to form the word "sun" (one syllable) and blending /f/ /l/ /ɑʊ/ /ɚ/ sounds to form the word "flower" (two syllables)
vocabulary.pragmatic_competences: Expressing connection with nature: Talking about sensory observations and experiences in nature (e.g., "I hear the birds." "The flowers smell nice.") Locating people and things: Providing directions or identifying locations in nature (e.g., "I am near the big tree." "We are at the park entrance.")
vocabulary.sociolinguistic_competences: Expressing appreciation for nature: Politely expressing feelings and preferences related to outdoor activities (e.g., "I like sitting under the tree. It's peaceful." "This is my favorite spot in the park."). Participating in polite requests: Using courteous phrases to interact with others during nature-related activities (e.g., "Can you pass me the binoculars, please?" "Would you like to sit here?").

skills_and_technology_integration.skills: Nature Awareness: Connecting with the outdoors. Communication: Using "can" and "can't" to describe abilities.
skills_and_technology_integration.technology_integration: Use a nature journaling app to document observations.

projects.name: Project 1: Nature Observation Journal
projects.overview: Students observe nature around school, writing sentences using "can" and "can't" to describe their abilities (e.g., "I can see a tree.").

projects.name: Project 2: Outdoor Role-Play
projects.overview: Students role-play outdoor activities using sentences like "I can relax." or "I can't hear the birds.".

projects.name: Project 3: Digital Nature Journal
projects.overview: Students use a nature journaling app to document observations and feelings about nature.

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can recognize sounds, syllables, familiar words, phrases, simple instructions and the main points of simple conversations when spoken slowly and clearly.
specific_standards: Receptive: Demonstrate comprehension of phrases with names and dates in a short, simple recording delivered at a slow pace.
Interactive: Present responses based on listened questions.
learning_outcomes: Can demonstrate understanding of familiar words and phrases with dates and numbers from recordings (e.g., "On Sunday, lunch is at 12.").
Can recognize familiar phrases with food names or numbers from simple recordings (e.g., "Three apples, two bananas").
Can create and present responses to questions about food preferences (e.g., "What's his favorite food?" "He likes apples.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can get the gist and main ideas of short texts if there are pictures.
specific_standards: Reading: Show comprehension of texts by answering questions, both written and oral.
Reading: Write responses to questions about a text.
Phonemic Awareness: Blend spoken phonemes to form one-syllable or two-syllable words if these words have been previously encountered.
learning_outcomes: Can show understanding of food preference texts by writing short responses (e.g., "What is his favorite food?" "He likes apples.").
Can answer questions in writing about food choices based on short texts. (e.g., "What is his favorite food?" "He likes Sancocho.").
Can combine individual phonemes to construct familiar one-syllable or two-syllable words, using prior knowledge of the words (e.g., blending /ˈæ-p-əl/ to form the word "apple").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can describe personal experiences and basic things using simple words and phrases.
specific_standards: Productive: Describe objects using basic words or phrases, provided they can prepare in advance.
Interactive: Interact with questions and answers about a classroom topic.
learning_outcomes: Can describe food items using basic phrases (e.g., "It's a red apple.").
Can ask and answer questions in simple discussions about food with peers (e.g., "What's your favorite food?" "I like ice cream.").
Can describe basic food items by following a model provided in advance (e.g., "I like bananas. They are sweet.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can write simple texts coherently, such as captions, instructions, or short notes, using familiar words.
specific_standards: Productive: Compose short texts using simple phrases and sentences.
Interactive: Respond to written questions from peers.
learning_outcomes: Can compose short texts for images of food with simple words (e.g., "This is my lunch.").
Can respond to written questions from peers about food choices (e.g., "Do you like bananas?" "Yes, I do.").
Can write short notes for a lunch order (e.g., "I want a hamburger.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can use compensation strategies such as interpretation, simplified language, gestures, and pictures, to communicate ideas.
specific_standards: Text: Simplify written instructions for peers.
Concept: Relate concepts to everyday scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Can simplify food-related instructions for peers by pointing and using simple words (e.g., pointing to an apple and saying "Take an apple.").
Can relate food vocabulary to everyday scenarios with gestures (e.g., points to lunch and says, "I eat chicken at lunch.").
Can support understanding of food-related words by rephrasing instructions (e.g., says, "pick food" while holding an apple).

grammatical_features: WH- and yes/no questions (e.g., "What's your favorite food?" "Do you like sancocho?")
Compound sentences with the conjunction but (e.g., "I like...but I don't...")

linguistic_competences.nouns: apple, banana, sandwich, lunch, breakfast, dinner, food, snack, water, juice, rice with chicken, soup
linguistic_competences.verbs: eat, drink, taste, choose, bring, want, enjoy, share, prepare, serve

vocabulary.pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness: Pronunciation: /f/ in "favorite" and /s/ in "snack". Phonemic awareness: Blending of spoken phonemes to form one-syllable and two-syllable familiar words related to food (e.g., /ˈæ-p.əl/ in "apple" and /ˈw-ɔːt-ər/ in "water")
vocabulary.pragmatic_competences: Asking for and giving information about preferences: Expressing likes and dislikes about food (e.g., "I like apples."), and asking about others' food preferences (e.g., "Do you like oranges?")
vocabulary.sociolinguistic_competences: Sharing preferences: Respectfully expressing likes and dislikes about food (e.g., "I like apples, but I am not a fan of broccoli.").

skills_and_technology_integration.skills: Social Interaction: Asking and answering questions about food preferences. Communication: Describing food preferences with "like".
skills_and_technology_integration.technology_integration: Use a digital survey tool to gather and graph class food preferences.

projects.name: Project 1: Favorite Food Survey
projects.overview: Students conduct a class survey asking peers about their favorite foods (e.g., "What's your favorite food?") and create a chart showing the results.

projects.name: Project 2: Food Recipe Book
projects.overview: Students create a simple recipe book by drawing pictures of their favorite foods and writing sentences like "I like sancocho.".

projects.name: Project 3: Digital Food Survey
projects.overview: Students use a digital survey tool to gather and make a graph of types of food preferences.

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can recognize sounds, syllables, familiar words, phrases, simple instructions and the main points of simple conversations when spoken slowly and clearly.
specific_standards: Receptive: Demonstrate comprehension of phrases with names and dates in a short, simple recording delivered at a slow pace.
Interactive: Perform tasks based on oral instructions.
learning_outcomes: Can demonstrate comprehension of familiar bedtime phrases with names and times from recordings (e.g., "It is time for bed!").
Can perform bedtime tasks from oral instructions (e.g., "It is time to brush your teeth.").
Can get the main points in short conversations about bedtime (e.g., "It is time to sleep.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can get the gist and main ideas of short texts if there are pictures.
specific_standards: Reading: Summarize a text using a graphic organizer.
Reading: Outline the meaning of simple paragraphs.
Phonemic Awareness: Blend spoken phonemes to form one-syllable or two-syllable words if these words have been previously encountered.
learning_outcomes: Can summarize bedtime routines in a graphic organizer (e.g., "First, I put on my pajamas. Then, I brush my teeth. Last, I go to bed.").
Can outline main ideas of bedtime stories with simple keywords (e.g., "sleep," "brush," and "night").
Can blend spoken phonemes to form one-syllable or two-syllable words related to daily routines (e.g., /wɔːʃ/ in the word "wash" and /t-iːθ/ in the word "teeth").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can describe personal experiences and basic things using simple words and phrases.
specific_standards: Productive: Express likes and dislikes.
Interactive: Respond to simple instructions during activities.
learning_outcomes: Can express preferences about bedtime (e.g., "I like bedtime stories.").
Can express preferences about personal bedtime routines (e.g., " I like to brush my teeth before I go to bed.").
Can follow and respond to instructions about bedtime (e.g., "Go to bed now." "Okay.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can write simple texts coherently, such as captions, instructions, or short notes, using familiar words.
specific_standards: Productive: Create descriptive captions for images with simple words.
Interactive: Edit a co-constructed text.
learning_outcomes: Can create captions for images of bedtime routines (e.g., "Time to sleep.").
Can edit and improve a co-constructed text about bedtime routines (e.g., revising "I brush my teeth." to "First, I brush my teeth. Then, I put on my pajamas. Last, I go to bed.").
Can write short phrases and sentences on bedtime routines collaboratively (e.g., "I am sleepy.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can use compensation strategies such as interpretation, simplified language, gestures, and pictures, to communicate ideas.
specific_standards: Text: Explain keywords from readings in simpler terms.
Concept: Explain simple events in story form.
learning_outcomes: Can explain keywords about bedtime routines using gestures (e.g., mimes sleeping for "sleep").
Can explain simple bedtime events in story form with basic actions (e.g., "First, I brush my teeth." and act it out).
Can guide peers in understanding bedtime routines by pointing to visuals (e.g., points to bed and says, "Sleep here.").
